newsitem.title: GERMANY: Study shows German maglev train unviable - report.
newsitem.headline: Study shows German maglev train unviable - report.

text.p: New projections show Germany's planned Transrapid high-speed train will have to charge much higher fares than previously believed, making the project uneconomic, the Handelsblatt newspaper reported on Wednesday.

The newspaper did not cite the source of its new data, but said it had copies of the report. A government study analysing the costs and viability of the magnetic levitation rail project is due for release at the end of March.
The total cost of the project is officially estimated at nine billion marks ($5.5 billion), but critics charge it will inevitably be much higher.
Handelsblatt said fares would have to be 0.47 to 0.60 marks per passenger-kilometer to break even, double the previous estimate of 0.28 marks.
It said private-sector participants in the Thyssen -led consortium planning the Transrapid would meet to consider the new data on Wednesday in Frankfurt.
Participants entering a conference room at Frankfurt airport said there would be a meeting about the Transrapid starting at 1500 GMT.
The participants declined to identify themselves, but referred journalists to the Handelsblatt report and declined to comment further.

A Transport Ministry spokesman said he had received no indications that private partners planned to pull out of the prestige project. Many questions remained open, and the available facts did not yet warrant a final decision, he said.

Last week, Transport Minister Matthias Wissmann said the government stood by its plans to build the controversial Transrapid, but that it would keep a close eye on it to prevent cost overruns. ($ = 1.642 German Marks)
